text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- The Yugoslav federal government decides to temporarily suspend imports of raw sugar and used tyres.
- Yugoslavia and Macedonia are discussing in Belgrade the signing of an inter-state agreement on pensions and welfare.
- The Belgrade construction firm Ivan Milutinovic signed a $4.5 million deal with Greece to build a marina in Rodos.
- The Yugoslav industry of machines and components IMK 14. Oktobar, Jugopetrol and Chinese company Simako signed a $38 million technical cooperation deal in Krusevac, central Serbia.

- Kragujevac car maker Zastava's delay in carrying out its production plan due to failure of its subcontractor from Rakovica 21 Maj to supply engines, says president of the Zastava group Srboljub Vasovic.
- Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic lays founding stone for new pharmaceutical plant within the premises of the Hemomont complex in Podgorica.
- Airport for commercial and sports aviation opened in Ecka near Zrenjanin Monday.
- International furniture fair opened in Belgrade on Monday, to last through November 17.

- Belgrade port Luka Beograd has handled 350,000 tonnes of goods in the first nine months of 1996, which is two and a half times more than last year but far below the pre-1991 volume, says director Miroslav Drobac.
- Yugoslav government is ready to facilitate access to personal documents for citizens of former Yugoslav republics.
- Car bomb explosion in central Belgrade demolishes car of private taxi copmany owner.
NASA BORBA
- The London Club of creditors is not satisfied with documentation provided by Yugoslavia on its development to the year 2005 and postpones talks until further notice.
- Delegation of the World Bank due to visit Belgrade on November 19 to present its report on world development not talk on Yugoslavia's status in the organisation.
- Succession talks on the former Yugoslavia continue in Brussels on Noveber 12 and 13, the Yugoslav stand remains unchanged.

- The executive board of the Association of Yugoslav Banks proposes half of the 15 percent banks' reserve requirement to be used for the purchase of wheat selling forward contracts, which would finance agriculture without igniting inflation.
- Belgrade lawyers, who will probably be joined by their lawyers elsewhere in Serbia, to stage new strike from November 15-22 over high taxes.
- Around 98 percent of children vaccinated in second round of polio vaccination in Serbia's Kosovo province.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- One worker killed and three injured in accident in Smederevo's steelworks Sartid 1913.

- Over the closure of the Trieste bank secretary of the Association of Yugoslav Banks Mileta Babovic suggests that all Yugoslav banks with deposits there form a club of creditors who will jointly appear before the recievership administrator.
BORBA

- Greek firm Gener SA and Banja Luka holding company Cajevec set up mixed company called Cajevac-Gener Engineering in Banja Luka, Bosnian Serb Republic under which four million dollars will be invested in telecommunications.
